## Steps

body:
@DevynCJohnson Thanks but I don't think your PR actually changes anything for your linked issues. As mentioned in https://github.com/PyCQA/pylint/pull/2537#discussion_r224197606, the current `master` should deal with all the linked issues, but your PR improves though a potential bug in `format.py` related to `line-too-long` and other additional linter comments.

issue.title: Make #novermin comments work better with other linter comments

repository.name: vermin
repository.description: Concurrently detect the minimum Python versions needed to run code

issue.body:
Sometimes we need to use multiple linter comments in one line (see also https://github.com/PyCQA/pylint/issues/2485). Consider the following code snippet, which has three linter comments in one line:

```python
import os

if hasattr(os, 'sched_getaffinity'):
    CPU_CNT = len(os.sched_getaffinity(0))  # type: ignore[attr-defined] # pylint: disable=no-member # novermin
else:
    ...
```

It would be good if everything works no matter how these comments are ordered, which is the current behavior of Pylint and Flake8. But for vermin, currently it only works (i.e. correctly exclude the line from analysis) when `# novermin` is the last comment. `# novermin # type: ignore[attr-defined] # pylint: disable=no-member` and `# type: ignore[attr-defined] # novermin # pylint: disable=no-member` do not work (for some reason Mypy requires the type comment to be the first comment, but that's not a vermin problem.)

I see [a relevant change](https://github.com/netromdk/vermin/commit/7a7a84245a50806f6c3b4708067dc1548eafa436) in the master branch. A caveat is that extracting comments with [this regular expression](https://github.com/netromdk/vermin/blob/7a7a84245a50806f6c3b4708067dc1548eafa436/vermin/parser.py#L6) may introduce false positive `# novermin` comments if `# novermin` happens to be in a string literal. Maybe using the [`tokenize`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/tokenize.html) module to detect `COMMENT` tokens is a better way.

**Environment**
 - Vermin version 0.10.3

issue.title: Can't use other comments after "# fmt: ..." (like "# noqa: ...")

labels.name: S: accepted
labels.description: The changes in this design / enhancement issue have been accepted and can be implemented

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

Hi, I am experiencing an issue with `# fmt: skip`. If I put it next to long line - this line will be skipped (as expected):
```python
log.debug("Long debug message ...........................................................")  # fmt: skip
```
But then flake8 will give me "E501 line too long" message, which I usually ignore with `# noqa: E501` comment, but using it together with `# fmt: skip` is impossible, line below will be formatted:
```python
log.debug("Long debug message, so we ignore flake8's E501 long line message")  # fmt: skip # noqa: E501
```

**To Reproduce**

1. Create file test.py:
```python
from logging import getLogger
log = getLogger("log")
log.debug("Long debug message, so we ignore flake8's E501 long line message")  # fmt: skip # noqa: E501
```
2. Run _Black_ on it
3. See that line was not skipped, but formatted

**Expected behavior**

I expected `black` to handle it just as `flake8` and `bandit`, they for example detect everything properly if I put both `# nosec # noqa` comments on the same line.

**Environment:**

- Version: 21.5b0
- OS and Python version: Ubuntu 18.04, Python 3.8.8

**Does this bug also happen on main?**

Yes, [online formatter link](https://black.vercel.app/?version=main&state=_Td6WFoAAATm1rRGAgAhARYAAAB0L-Wj4ADvAKhdAD2IimZxl1N_WlkPinBFoKDF2jxVGq6-OkJfExE4EFK1Ba2QEEWxG3L6cfu_uSU05A1Vcy0SB5pxSv-o5TU7MpxzIWRnm0Irtmk7pulh2jJeWvPzvmzIfNFpAIlQYsqtws3RBwrPUJEbQ68dZ2NEOAaJfDLLidp2rqkvD-FaLwssdMISvf3FOFRaqjba0iQf01vyL9TyYbt2Ppzw02L7akOjNmE7oqFhAACuKveKZxRh-AABxAHwAQAAX93o87HEZ_sCAAAAAARZWg==)

issue.title: checks: Flake8 F841 fixes in the wxpython directory part 3

milestone.description: JSON output for many tools, MkDocs documentation with Markdown source code, and other new features

repository.name: grass
repository.description: GRASS - free and open-source geospatial processing engine

issue.body:
## Description
Flake8 F841 (local variable assigned to but never used) fixes in the `gui/wxpython/gpc` and `gui/wxpython/gui_core` directory.

## Motivation and context
Changes require resolving a part of Flake8 warnings that are currently ignored. The issue title and number as follows.

- [Bug] Fix currently ignored Flake8 warnings https://github.com/OSGeo/grass/issues/1522
## How has this been tested?
**g.gui.gpc**: Briefly tested using GUI and worked fine
**gui_core**:  N/A 

## Types of changes
- Removed unused variables and lines to fix F841.
- Replaced `# pylint: disable=W0612` with `# noqa: F841` in `gui_core/treeview.py`. Please let me know if you want to keep "# pylint". It looks a little odd, but adding `# noqa:` to the end of code doesn't work. It must be the first line with multiline, like below.

```python
    n111 = tree.AppendNode(  # noqa: F841
        parent=n11, data={"label": "node111", "xxx": "A"}
    )
```
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as before)

## Checklist
- [x] PR title provides summary of the changes and starts with one of the [pre-defined prefixes](https://github.com/OSGeo/grass/blob/main/utils/release.yml)
- [x] My code follows the [code style](https://github.com/OSGeo/grass/blob/main/doc/development/style_guide.md) of this project.
 - [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation.
-  [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly.
-  [ ] I have added tests to cover my changes.
